translation.text: The words of Enoch’s blessing, with which he blessed the chosen and righteous who will be present on the day of distress, when all the evil and godless are removed.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected removal phrase applies to the evil and godless, not to the chosen and righteous. Actual Dillmann cols349–350 gives removal or expulsion for the verb and col681 distress for the day-expression. The two condemned descriptions are retained without asserting two separately identified populations.

translation.text: Enoch answered and said—a righteous man from God, [while] his eyes were open, and he saw a holy vision in the heavens, which the angels showed me. I heard everything from them, and I understood—I, †what I see†—not for this generation, but for a distant one to come.[a]

footnotes.text: The third-person description, first-person showing/hearing clauses, bracketed while, and daggered seeing phrase are retained as difficulties, not silently rewritten as a uniformly first-person speech. Charles printed2note14 discusses corruption in the daggered phrase and possible repairs; no repair or seer-title substitution is adopted. This whole proposed unit is held.

translation.text: Concerning the chosen I spoke, and I uttered a parable about them: the Holy and Great One will come out from his dwelling.[a]

footnotes.text: The speech verb can mean answer or begin/utter a discourse, checked in actual Dillmann col895, while the parable noun is checked at col173. The about/on-behalf-of construction is checked at cols775–776. This is a selected Ethiopic construal, not a silent replacement from a familiar Greek or English opening.

translation.text: The God of eternity will tread from there upon Mount Sinai. He will appear in his encampment, and he will appear from heaven in the strength of his might.[a]

footnotes.text: Actual Dillmann col1007 gives camp/encampment and host or army senses for the selectedትዕይንትword; it is not merely a generic word for manifestation. “With his host” is another possible rendering. The motion/treading range is checked in col872. No Greek camp-reading has been imported into an unrelated Ethiopic word.

translation.text: All will fear, and the Watchers will tremble. Fear and great trembling will seize them as far as the ends of the earth.[a]

footnotes.text: The selectedትጉሃንis the wakeful or vigilant Watchers term, explicitly checked in actual Dillmann col572. The inherited note claiming that this was not the usual Watchers word is not retained. The trembling and seizing clauses are checked at cols1078,312 and635–636.

translation.text: The earth will sink, and everything in the earth will be destroyed. Judgment will come upon all.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected verb isወትሰጥም, not the inherited rent-asunder transcription. Actual Dillmann col400 cites Enoch1:7 under sinking/submergence. “Sink” retains that meaning without adding an unstated flood or a new prediction about modern geography. The complete destruction and universal judgment clauses remain.

translation.text: He will make peace for the righteous and guard the chosen. Mercy will be upon them, and they will all belong to God. They will prosper and be blessed, and God’s light will shine for them.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected opening bracketed phrase, literally “for all the righteous, all of them,” duplicates the surrounding righteous expressions; Charles printed4note9 calls it a dittography. The complete bracketed words remain in the source, while English expresses their repeated meaning once. This is an explicit critical treatment, not a claim of missing ancient text. Mercy, prosperity, guarding and light are checked at actual Dillmann cols229–230,237,977–978 and499–500.

translation.text: Look, he comes with myriads of holy ones, to carry out judgment ⟦the daggered object remains unresolved⟧, destroy the godless, and reprove all flesh concerning everything they did and set against him, sinners [and] godless ones.[a]
